questions.stem: Compressed paraffin sections are best addressed first by:

choices.text: Cooling the block and checking blade sharpness
Raising the bath above wax melting point

questions.explanation: A cool block and sharp blade are common first corrections for compression.

questions.stem: Regular alternating thick and thin sections are called:
questions.explanation: Periodic thick-thin variation is often termed Venetian blind artifact and may reflect mechanical instability or block/blade factors.

questions.stem: For a small GI biopsy, the preferred embedding approach is to:

choices.text: Align mucosal surfaces consistently in one plane
Embed all fragments vertically without inspection

questions.explanation: Consistent alignment helps obtain complete representative sections at similar cutting depth.

questions.stem: Sections detach from charged slides during harsh retrieval. A useful first review includes:

choices.text: Slide type, drying, section adhesion, and retrieval conditions

questions.explanation: Adhesion failures can reflect slide chemistry, contamination, inadequate drying, tissue type, or overly harsh retrieval.

questions.stem: The flotation bath is used primarily to:
questions.explanation: Warm water relaxes compression and wrinkles so a flat section can be collected.

questions.stem: The flotation bath temperature should generally be:

choices.text: A few degrees below the paraffin melting point
Identical for every wax formulation without validation

questions.explanation: The bath should flatten sections without melting paraffin or causing expansion artifacts.

questions.stem: A ribbon repeatedly splits at the same point. The most likely local cause is:

choices.text: A nick in the blade or hard material in the block

questions.explanation: A blade defect or focal hard material can repeatedly disrupt the ribbon at the same location.

questions.stem: When cutting scrolls for molecular testing, the most important contamination control is to:

choices.text: Use the same uncleaned blade for all cases
Use clean tools and case-specific contamination precautions
Float scrolls on a shared water bath
Handle all blocks with bare hands

questions.explanation: Clean equipment, fresh blade areas, and controlled handling reduce cross-contamination of molecular samples.

questions.stem: A regressive hematoxylin method relies on:
questions.explanation: Regressive methods intentionally overstain nuclei, then remove excess hematoxylin selectively.

questions.stem: After acid-alcohol differentiation, nuclei are reddish-purple. The next required step is:
questions.explanation: Bluing converts hematoxylin to its stable blue form in an alkaline environment.
